his_words: catégorie abélienne; Tous ces foncteurs sont fidèles
statement: The outline postulates a semisimple rational category of effective pure motives with tensor product and faithful classical realizations; it does not construct the correspondence quotient or prove its properties.
reconstruction: Numerical, homological, absolute-Hodge, motivated and Nori motives are different candidates. Numerical semisimplicity cannot supply the missing faithful realization without further cycle conjectures.
check_reason: N001 and N090 correctly distinguish the proposed category from a theorem. No equivalence relation is filled in from the absent cote16 context.

statement: The effective pure weight-one part is contravariantly equivalent to abelian varieties over k up to isogeny, with Picard/dual-abelian conventions retained.
reconstruction: For actual homological or motivated constructions this means the subcategory generated by h1, with rational morphisms; it is not an equivalence with all integral abelian schemes.
check_reason: The superscript opposite and the dual abelian variety matter; neither can be dropped.

his_words: pleinement fidèle; invariante par extension du corps de base
statement: The outline asserts full faithfulness for algebraically closed field extension. A later sentence asserting invariance of level and pure level under base extension is cancelled.
reconstruction: Full faithfulness of a chosen motive category and invariance of a proposed filtration are separate statements; neither implies essential surjectivity.
check_reason: N003 is retained; N010 correctly records cancellation at scan3, not withdrawal of every base-extension assertion on scan2.

statement: Tensor functors from the proposed motive category to a pseudo-abelian tensor category are claimed to correspond to contravariant functors on smooth projective varieties satisfying Künneth and invertibility of the P1 projector image.
reconstruction: A correct universal correspondence construction must specify cycle classes, equivalence relation and compatibility with composition/duality. Künneth and invertibility alone are not a complete presentation.
check_reason: The note correctly identifies missing data instead of importing a later universal theorem.

his_words: Tout motif ... se décompose ... de façon unique
statement: Level≤i is defined by Tate twisting an effective object with homogeneous degrees≤i. In the proposed semisimple category, summing simple constituents of each minimal level gives a unique pure-level decomposition.
reconstruction: The argument needs finite length, a well-defined nonnegative minimum and the chosen effective subcategory. It is not the mixed-weight filtration.
check_reason: The notes correctly read a level decomposition and keep its dependence on the conjectural category.

statement: For a pure weight-n object with an effective primitive weight-i constituent, the modern convention wt(M(r))=wt(M)-2r requires twist (i-n)/2.
reconstruction: This is an index alarm only. Pro marks the sign/order uncertain; Codex reads (n-i)/2. The ink may use another convention or contain an error.
check_reason: The antitwist Q(-1) has weight2 elsewhere, so silently choosing the modern sign would change the witness.

statement: For smooth projective X and a suitable smooth complete-intersection section Y of dimension i≤dim X, weak Lefschetz gives an injection H^i(X)→H^i(Y). A motivic injection and splitting require the chosen motivic formalism and semisimplicity.
reconstruction: The cohomological theorem does not by itself manufacture an algebraic projector or correspondence inverse.
check_reason: The note preserves the distinction between a realized injection and its motivic lift.

statement: For smooth projective X, the geometric coniveau filtration on H^i is identified, under resolution and the standard-conjecture framework, with the largest submotive of level≤i−2j. The resulting dimensions are expected independent of ell.
reconstruction: The following word poids for successive level i−2j is inconsistent with pure cohomological weight i unless interpreted as level. The text itself gives conditional hypotheses and a marginal place for Tate/Hodge.
check_reason: Do not convert the conditional identification into an unconditional modern coniveau theorem or identify level with weight.

statement: A rigid abelian symmetric K-linear tensor category with End(1)=K and an exact faithful fibre functor to finite-dimensional K-vector spaces is reconstructed from its affine tensor-automorphism group. Tensor generation corresponds to finite type; characteristic-zero semisimplicity to pro-reductivity. Exterior/symmetric operations are intrinsic.
reconstruction: Rigidity, symmetry and exactness are made explicit; the manuscript shorthand connexe refers to End(1), not connectedness of the group.
check_reason: These are identifiable Tannakian claims; the finite-generation and characteristic-zero qualifications are actually on the page.

statement: For a regular integral base S the proposed pure-motive category uses generic-fibre correspondences, embeds fully faithfully in M(eta), and is asserted contravariantly functorial for morphisms of regular bases.
reconstruction: Specialization of generic correspondences along a nondominant map is extra structure; a generic cycle alone has no automatic pullback. Later relative motive theories use their own hypotheses.
check_reason: The marginal flag is retained; regularity is not treated as an unstated proof of specialization.

statement: Isomorphisms of fibre functors form a torsor, and changing fibre twists the group by an inner form. A tensor-generated Tannakian category can be neutralized over a finite coefficient-field extension.
reconstruction: The last assertion requires Tannakian existence, not merely arbitrary rigidity and symmetry: super-vector spaces with their usual symmetry show the missing positivity condition. A finite-type torsor has a closed point over a finite extension.
check_reason: The notes correctly distinguish torsor comparison from the existence of a first fibre functor and preserve the finite-generation restriction.

statement: How do the reductive groups obtained from different complex Betti base points compare? They are forms related by the fibre-functor isomorphism torsor, without a canonical rational trivialization.
reconstruction: Identifying a path or comparison is additional data; isomorphic complex realizations do not imply canonically identical rational groups.
check_reason: The question concerns comparison of realizations, not recovery of the base variety.

statement: A rational fibre functor with the expected dimensions cannot exist for all pure motives in characteristic p: a supersingular elliptic curve gives a quaternion division endomorphism algebra acting on a purported two-dimensional Q-space.
reconstruction: The algebra argument forces a four-dimensional division algebra to be M2(Q), impossible. Ell-adic fibres for ell≠p and finite coefficient extensions on finitely generated pieces are separate statements.
check_reason: The supplied witness explicitly names Serre; this is not evidence that the obstruction concerns period transcendence.

statement: Association of a fibre functor with a geometric point is a chosen tensor isomorphism on the Artin subcategory. Betti and Tate fibres have such data; de Rham need not be associated over its original coefficient field.
reconstruction: Existence and a chosen identification differ. The countability qualification at the algebraically closed-base example is retained as written, not promoted to a universal descent assertion.
check_reason: The note accurately preserves this extra datum.

his_words: Utilisant conjecture de Tate (ou de Hodge
statement: An initial unconditional component-group isomorphism is cancelled. The surviving text obtains an Artin quotient G→pi1 and an epimorphism pi0(G)→pi1, and invokes Tate/Hodge to make it an isomorphism. Connected finite étale covers correspond to inverse images of open subgroups.
reconstruction: Geometric-kernel exactness, geometric connectedness and the identity-component assertion are three distinct propositions. Finite-cover descent and subobject closure must be present in a modern reconstruction.
check_reason: N017–019 correctly separate the levels. The earlier boundary claim is updated: the alleged out-of-packet early leaves are supplied in this consolidated run.

reconstruction: This is a continuous section on rational points of a proalgebraic group, not automatically an algebraic group-scheme splitting.
check_reason: The distinction is explicit in N020 and confirmed by the types of all displayed arrows.

statement: Over a localization of a finite-type Z-scheme, Tate fullness together with semisimplicity is expressed as Zariski density of the ell-adic Galois image in finite motivic quotients. A marginal semi-invariant formulation is proposed to imply semisimplicity using standard conjectures.
reconstruction: Equality of tensor invariants reconstructs a group only with the stated Tannakian hypotheses. The marginal half-invariant shorthand is not silently normalized.
check_reason: The earlier notes rightly retain the semisimplicity insertion and the conditional margin.

statement: Over a finite field, Frobenius is a central tensor automorphism. Under the stated Tate-density and semisimplicity framework, its Zariski closure is the motivic group, which is commutative and an extension of the proconstant arithmetic quotient by a protorus.
reconstruction: The centre is then the entire group, not trivial. The struck canonical-triviality qualification is not restored.
check_reason: N023–024 properly keep conditional commutativity separate from any statement about a project centre.

statement: A closed finite-residue-field point should define a rational conjugacy invariant of Frobenius in the invariant quotient of a motivic group; for a connected reductive group this quotient is T/W.
reconstruction: The rationality and independence of the fibre form are motivic assertions. T/W requires reductivity and connectedness; rational invariant classes need not give rational conjugating elements.
check_reason: The note does not confuse a quotient point with a distinguished representative in G(Q).

statement: A functorial grading on the tensor category yields a central weight cocharacter. A nontrivial Lefschetz sl2 Cartan cannot literally be this central element because [H,L]=2L.
reconstruction: The obstruction is an independent check of the earlier-run proposed bridge. The external LM6 A.22 normalizer problem remains an attributed lead, not a theorem about motives.
check_reason: The centrality is on the page; the comparison with Lefschetz and LM is explicitly external.

statement: Hodge bidegree gives commuting cocharacters i1,i2 whose product is the central total weight. The Tate character on Q(-1) evaluates the weight cocharacter as t².
reconstruction: Complex conjugation of cocharacters must include the argument convention. Pro/Codex signs/bars remain an ink question.
check_reason: The square is fixed by the explicitly stated weight2 of Q(-1).

statement: A filtered fibre functor, once locally split, differs from its graded fibre by a torsor under the unipotent group of filtration-preserving automorphisms trivial on the associated graded.
reconstruction: The page assumes local existence of a splitting; it does not prove it. Define the group as the kernel of the graded-action morphism.
check_reason: The missing construction and the assumed extension are retained.

statement: Polarizable pure rational Hodge structures form a semisimple tensor category. A real invariant form alone need not be a positive polarization.
reconstruction: The counterform diag(1,−1) disproves the proposed implication from real invariance to positivity; it is not an assertion made by Grothendieck here.
check_reason: N029/N096 correctly keep real structure, Hodge symmetry and positivity distinct.

statement: The Mumford–Tate group is the smallest Q-group containing the Hodge cocharacters; it is connected, and its invariant rational tensors are Hodge tensors. Hodge fullness on all tensor constructions identifies it with the corresponding algebraic-cycle motivic group.
reconstruction: G0 here names a motivic group, not its identity component. The final positivity heading is empty, not a completed proof.
check_reason: The notes state the tensor-closure condition needed to turn equality of invariants into equality of groups.

statement: The contents leaf lists nineteen topics, from M+(X) to Hodge cohomology, with a marginal coefficient-generalization instruction.
reconstruction: Nineteen is the number of outline headings, not a page count or count of completed sections. No date is written here.
check_reason: A programme is not promoted into nineteen completed constructions.

statement: The new general-base programme asks for a rational abelian effective category on noetherian schemes, right-exact tensor, bounded derived operations, exact pullback, and Rf* for f finite type with f proper OR Y excellent, plus projection and exceptional-duality identities.
reconstruction: These are proposed axioms, not a construction of an abelian heart. Modern triangulated six-functor categories realize part of the programme with their own finiteness hypotheses.
check_reason: The disjunction is explicit. A six-operations theorem is not evidence that a general motivic t-structure is established.

statement: Motives and direct images of descended finite-type data are required to commute with essentially affine inverse limits, reducing general bases to finite-type Z-models.
reconstruction: A filtered 2-colimit of categories and a comparison for an object descended to a finite stage are the modern meanings; qcqs/finite-presentation restrictions must be stated.
check_reason: The note correctly treats continuity as an axiom whose proof is absent.

his_words: exact et fidèle (mais non pleinement fidèle)
statement: When ell is invertible on X, realization into constructible Qell sheaves is required to be tensor, exact, faithful and compatible with pullback, direct images, Künneth and exceptional operations.
reconstruction: Faithfulness detects equality and, for an exact functor, detects isomorphisms of already constructed maps. It does not create a missing motivic map. Unit and cohomology compatibility exclude the zero category.
check_reason: The parenthetical non-fullness and the unit obstruction are literal. N038 is an earlier-run proof audit, not a new manuscript theorem.

statement: A proposed exact faithful coherent realization over Q-schemes compatible with pullback and Rf* is cancelled on the same leaf.
reconstruction: No later coherent or de Rham theory is used to reinstate the cancelled statement.
check_reason: The whole displayed construction lies inside deletion markup.

statement: The effective anti-Tate object is h²(P1). For smooth projective morphisms with nonempty geometrically connected fibres of dimension d, top direct image is Q(−d); the smooth quasi-projective compact-support version is also asserted.
reconstruction: The trace map must be constructed before realization proves it an isomorphism. Coefficient Q/Z marks remain diplomatic variants.
check_reason: The smoothness, geometric connectedness, nonemptiness and support convention are all necessary parts of the source.

statement: For a regular closed immersion of codimension d, absolute purity in derived conventions is Ri!1X≃1Y(−d)[−2d]. The displayed source lacks the shift.
reconstruction: The missing [−2d] is proposed for scan checking, not inserted into the transcription.

statement: Full faithfulness of effective Tate tensoring permits formal inversion by a filtered category of twists. Each object is M_n(n), with M_n effective for sufficiently large n and M_(n+1)≃M_n(−1).
reconstruction: The Q(+1) at one effective transition conflicts with the later Q(−1) arrows; the categorical localization is formal conditional on cancellation, not a proof of cancellation.

his_words: On retrouve la formation des f!

reconstruction: This concerns realizations of the same object, not arbitrary unrelated compatible systems; lisse does not mean finite monodromy.
check_reason: The interpretation is anchored by the actual realization comparison, not by a modern definition supplied silently.

his_words: à inclure dans le formalisme tensoriel
statement: An endomorphism of a dualizable motive has categorical trace in End(1)=Q. Tensor realizations preserve it; applying this to exterior powers gives a rational ell-independent characteristic polynomial.
reconstruction: Dualizability, contraction and the unit-endomorphism axiom must be available; the contraction is expressly flagged as missing.
check_reason: The trace computation is valid under these hypotheses and does not prove them.

statement: The effective category is filtered by fibrewise weight bounds, detected at closed points on finite-type arithmetic models; compact direct image shifts the upper bound by its cohomological degree. Pure geometric pieces are expected generated by smooth projective cohomology.
reconstruction: Mixed realizations have weight filtrations, while existence of the stated abelian motivic filtration remains additional. Generation indices on scan32 are uncertain; no universal decomposition is inferred.
check_reason: The later Frobenius criterion supplies the promised arithmetic test; the finite-type model cannot be omitted.

statement: Inverting Tate extends the weight filtration to integer indices; twist by Q(−j) shifts weight by 2j. Effective inclusions are generally strict. Associated pure quotients are identified within each parity, not necessarily all with weight zero.
reconstruction: If the doubtful subscript is 2i the last claim is coherent; if i it misses the odd class. Both readings are left open.
check_reason: The note correctly treats parity as dependent on a live transcription question.

statement: Early dimension type D is the smallest thick Tate-stable enlargement of bounded effective weights; all Tate objects have D-level0. Compact direct-image bounds are asserted, ordinary direct images and internal Ext bounds questioned.
reconstruction: This D is not the D-prime geometric-dimension filtration of scan45 or the later generating-dimension convention of scan125. The internal-Ext indices are not securely identifiable.

his_words: sur cette catégorie les Exti ... sont nuls
statement: Constant-twisted objects are asserted extension-stable, finite-length and tensor/internal-Hom closed; the accompanying higher-Ext vanishing is ambiguous between internal Ext of locally free objects and global extensions.
reconstruction: Global Ext1 of general lisse/mixed objects need not vanish: Kummer extensions give an obstruction. A pure semisimple interpretation or internal Ext meaning may be intended.
check_reason: N058 correctly preserves ambiguity and does not refute a local statement with a global example.

statement: The Grothendieck group of a finite-length abelian category is free on simple isomorphism classes. A fully faithful exact Tate shift preserving simples acts injectively on that basis; its class is therefore a non-zero-divisor and its inversion gives the non-effective group.
reconstruction: This is the Grothendieck ring of a motive category, not K0 of varieties, where the Lefschetz class has different behaviour.
check_reason: The argument is formal and the precise ring is essential.

statement: Purity of tensor products would refine the simple-object weight filtration to a grading. The ensuing descriptions use degree1 for Tate and polynomial notation although Tate is invertible.
reconstruction: With the earlier weight convention, Tate has degree2 and non-effective even/odd pieces use Laurent powers. A rescaled even grading must be declared explicitly.
check_reason: The notes identify an unresolved mixture of conventions, not an established normalized presentation.

statement: The proposed primitive set subtracts all Tate-divisible pieces; the written alpha≥0 subtracts the set itself. After replacing it conjecturally by alpha≥1, simple classes partition into Tate strings. Their multiplication still requires structure constants.
reconstruction: For the early D-filtration, gr_D_i is generated by all Tate translates of primitives of level i, not by the displayed weight-i sum. Both index repairs are mathematical proposals only.
check_reason: The zero-term contradiction and the independent multiplicative data are checked directly.

statement: The page promises the low-level primitive classification, predicts Tate-adjusted duality fixes primitive classes using positivity, and asks for lambda operations through finite operator groups.
reconstruction: Artin/Tate and weight-one abelian pieces address low levels in appropriate categories. Self-duality requires polarizability; defining exterior powers is distinct from computing the decomposition of every primitive tensor operation.
check_reason: These are three separately tracked open steps attached to the same primitive-ring object, not a completed ring calculation.

statement: Test the competing gradings on the unit, Tate line and h1 of an elliptic curve before using any primitive-ring formula.

check_reason: The test is attributed to the earlier run and does not become a conjecture of the author.

his_words: Attention, terme initial E1 et non E2 !!
statement: The coniveau spectral sequence has E1^(p,q)=sum over codimension-p points H^(q−p)(k(x))(−p), and a motivic lift is sought from E2 or in Ind-motives. For projective smooth X it should identify level pieces.
reconstruction: The source alternates n−2p and n−p, and restores projectivity after deleting it. E1 terms do not identify the abutment without differentials or degeneration.
check_reason: The note accurately retains the author’s E1 correction, projectivity reservation and the unresolved index.

statement: A cancelled coniveau extension with twisted coefficients and a dense-open box precede a surviving assertion: H^i(X)→H^i(U) has kernel of level≤i−2 and cokernel of level≤i−1 for smooth X and dense U, under the proposed formalism.
reconstruction: Localization/purity explain these different bounds. Smoothness is questioned, not removed; resolving or altering models is an additional input.
check_reason: Both the withdrawn and surviving formulations are recorded so cancellation is not confused with later contradiction.

statement: The scissors ring of finite-type varieties maps to the motive Grothendieck ring by compact Euler characteristic sum(−1)^i[Hc^i]. Weight components give signed virtual Betti numbers.
reconstruction: Additivity needs the localization triangle and multiplicativity Künneth. Weight degree is not automatically cohomological degree on a nonproper variety.
check_reason: The map is conditional on the programme but is the familiar motivic-measure construction in established realization theories.

statement: The first injectivity/surjectivity question is crossed out and replaced by the D-prime filtration adapted to geometric dimension. Its top quotient gives gamma_n+xi gamma_(n−1)+..., of weights n,n+1,..., with an explicit sign reservation.
reconstruction: D-prime differs from the early Tate-stable D. The wholly cancelled scan52 returns to an injectivity question; it is not evidence of a final accepted conjecture.
check_reason: The notes correctly preserve revisions, the weight arithmetic and the sign caveat.

his_words: si ... n’est pas dominant ... est nul
statement: A birational object is defined as the largest bipure subobject of the dense-open cohomology limit; dominant pullback should be injective. The same passage says every nondominant map acts by zero.
reconstruction: Finite existence in an Ind-object is unproved. Functoriality for all morphisms plus zero on every nondominant map is impossible: a section C→C×P1 and projection compose to id while the section would induce zero.
check_reason: The earlier retraction test is reproduced, conditional only on a nonzero gamma1(C). The claim can be restricted to dominant rational maps.

statement: The stated faithfulness wish actually asks every system of maps between gamma-invariants to lift to a field embedding after adjoining transcendental variables, and mutual embeddability from isomorphic invariant systems.
reconstruction: Without admissibility, zero maps cannot arise from dominant embeddings. Polynomial brackets must mean rational function fields for genuine stabilization, since units force every field homomorphism into a polynomial ring to land in its constant field. Mutual embeddings do not assert stable birational equivalence.
check_reason: The note’s terminology correction and bracket alarm are both necessary.

his_words: un hom J→Jprime à noyau fini
statement: Over an algebraically closed field, an isogeny of Jacobians is asked to yield a dominant rational map from a curve times affine space to the other curve.
reconstruction: In characteristic0 Howe’s geometrically nonisomorphic genus2 curves with isomorphic unpolarized Jacobians disprove this. A rational map from a rational fibre to a genus2 curve is constant, so stabilization does not avoid Riemann–Hurwitz.
check_reason: Hua’s cited counterexample lead is independently checked; no principal-polarization compatibility was present in the manuscript.

statement: The page asks whether vanishing of all positive gamma-invariants, in particular entirely algebraic cohomology, forces unirationality.
reconstruction: For i>0 and rational homological motives over C, an Enriques surface has motive 1+10Q(−1)+Q(−2), so all positive bipure pieces vanish while Kodaira dimension0 excludes unirationality. This does not infer a Chow-motive decomposition merely from Betti numbers.
check_reason: The i>0 versus i≥0 ink ambiguity and the motivic interpretation are explicit conditions of the counterexample.

statement: The quotient of the dimension-graded scissors group by ruled classes is compared with top bipure motives. The consequence that algebraic H2 forces a surface to be ruled is rejected by the author using E×E with E supersingular.
reconstruction: Here b2=6 and all degree2 classes are algebraic, but an abelian surface has no rational curves. Its H1 is nonzero, so it is not an example for vanishing of every positive gamma. Larsen–Lunts concerns a different whole-ring quotient by the affine line.
check_reason: The negative answer and its exact scope are in the margin; the broader quotient question is not settled by naming a related theorem.
